label: sec:speed-of-light-intro
html:
Having established the Reeb-flow operational entropy and the Planck step, we now extract a velocity and a mass--energy law. The q-connection on the state bundle, operating at the substrate parameter q_0, natively defines a Lieb--Robinson cone for information propagation. This causal cone forms the physical speed of light.

The speed of light emerges as the Lieb--Robinson velocity c_q = 1/(q-1). This bounds the maximum information bandwidth per Planck step. A rigorous mass--energy equivalence (E_{\mathfrak{H}} = \mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{H}} \cdot c_q^2) follows immediately by evaluating the categorical trace of the crossing energy within the ribbon category. Mass \mathfrak{m} assumes a Gröbner–Shirshov interpretation: it quantifies the topological cost of threading a photon through a knot. Subsequently, the gravitational constant G_q aligns with Jacobson's entropy--area derivation via information geometry. The Hausdorff dimension d_H(q) = (2q-1)^2/q^3 directly governs the discrete recurrence, saturating the Margolus--Levitin bound. These parameters—c_q and the bandwidth budget \mathfrak{B}(q)—will strictly bound every Toffoli step.
